name: Boeing 757
summary: Long, powerful single-aisle twin flown by Delta and United and as a freighter by FedEx and UPS; the USAF flies a handful as the C-32A.

wings: Swept low wing that looks short for the long fuselage
Many US airframes have tall blended winglets; others have plain tips
engines: Two very large turbofans (RB211 or PW2000) for a narrowbody, hung far forward of the wing
fuselage: Very long, slender 6-abreast fuselage (the -300 even longer)
Tall landing gear gives a nose-high, stalky stance
Droopy pointed nose with a sloping six-pane windshield
tail: Tall swept fin with a straight leading edge

tellTales: Long thin pencil-like fuselage on tall stilt-like gear
Big engines on a single-aisle body

confusedWith.howToTell: The 757 is long and slender with a single aisle and four-wheel bogies on tall gear; the 767 is a short, fat twin-aisle widebody.
The 757 is far longer with tall gear, much larger engines and a droopy pointed nose; the A321 sits low with a blunt rounded nose.
The 757 is much longer with tall gear and huge engines; the 737 sits low with flat-bottomed engine intakes.
